Baked Bangor Oysters with Garlic Herb Butter

Served at: Feast of St. Muirgen (Lí Ban the Mermaid)

Serves 4-6 as an appetizer (12 oysters)Prep 25 minCook 10-12 min

For the Feast of St. Muirgen, also known as Lí Ban the Mermaid, these baked oysters pay homage to the sea and the saint's origins. This recipe features fresh oysters baked with a savory garlic-herb butter and a hint of breadcrumbs for texture, offering a warm and celebratory dish perfect for honoring the patroness of the waters.

Ingredients

  • 12 fresh oysters, preferably from a cold-water region, scrubbed clean
  • 1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, finely chopped
  • 1 tablespoon fresh chives, finely chopped
  • 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • Pinch of sea salt (optional)
  • 2 tablespoons panko breadcrumbs
  • Lemon wedges, for serving
  • Rock salt or crumpled aluminum foil, for serving

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
  2. Carefully shuck the oysters, detaching the oyster from the bottom shell but leaving it in its shell. Discard the top shell. Arrange the oysters in their half shells on a baking sheet, using rock salt or crumpled aluminum foil to keep them stable.
  3. In a small bowl, combine the softened butter, minced garlic, chopped parsley, chopped chives, lemon juice, black pepper, and salt (if using). Mix until well combined.
  4. Spoon about 1 teaspoon of the garlic-herb butter mixture over each oyster.
  5. Sprinkle a small amount of breadcrumbs over each buttered oyster.
  6. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the edges of the oysters begin to curl and the butter is bubbling. Do not overcook.
  7. Carefully remove from the oven. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges.

Tips

  • If shucking oysters is daunting, ask your fishmonger to shuck them for you, requesting they leave them in their bottom shells.
  • For an extra touch of richness, a tablespoon of grated Parmesan cheese can be sprinkled over the breadcrumbs before baking.
  • Ensure oysters are fresh; they should smell briny and clean, not fishy.
